name: F Minor

global_influences.artist_or_genre: Indigenous folk traditions of Bangladesh (Garo, Marma)
global_influences.evidence: The band's members are drawn from the Garo and Marma communities and the folk music of those communities is described as its foremost influence — a local rather than global influence vector, and one absent from every other act in this catalogue.
global_influences.source: The Daily Star, 'F Minor: Winning hearts through diversity and rhythm'; The Business Standard, "F Minor's fusion of ethnic and folk music"

local_adaptation_notes: Inverts the usual direction of the local-adaptation question. Where most acts in this catalogue take a global form and localise it, F Minor takes indigenous-community repertoire — from communities marginal to the Bangla-language mainstream — and arranges it for a band format. Its songs foreground women's rights and recognition, and the band frames its work as being for women's rights broadly, not only for indigenous communities.
sound_evolution_summary: Launched October 2016; band-format arrangements (guitar, keys, cajon) of Garo and Marma folk material alongside covers in other genres.
concert_culture_notes: Opened the main slate of the sixth Joy Bangla Concert (2020) at the Bangladesh Army Stadium, described in coverage as the country's first all-female folk band; also performs at indigenous cultural events such as Wangala.
listener_community_notes: Reaches an audience that the rock/metal and pop strands do not: the band's visibility is tied to cultural-plurality and women's-rights framing as much as to genre affiliation.
